library_findings.relevant_api: tree_sitter_php::LANGUAGE constant; grammar node types: class_declaration, interface_declaration, trait_declaration, enum_declaration, method_declaration, function_definition, use_statement, base_clause, class_interface_clause
library_findings.notes: Official tree-sitter-php grammar from tree-sitter/tree-sitter-php repo. Grammar uses base_clause (extends) and class_interface_clause (implements) as separate child nodes, not fields of class_declaration. Method declarations are inside declaration_list body. Functions are function_definition, not method_declaration. Interfaces, traits, enums all have declaration_list bodies. See php/src/node-types.json for authoritative field names.

library_findings.relevant_api: Query syntax for tree-sitter patterns; child_by_field_name(), named_child(), child_count() for tree traversal
library_findings.notes: Workspace dependency already pinned to 0.27.1; tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 is compatible with this version

approaches.name: Full OO Handler with Inheritance (Recommended)
approaches.description: Create crates/aptu-coder-core/src/languages/php.rs with all five query constants (ELEMENT_QUERY covering functions, methods, classes, interfaces, traits, enums; CALL_QUERY for method/function calls; REFERENCE_QUERY for type references; IMPORT_QUERY for use statements; DEFUSE_QUERY for local variables and assignments). Implement extract_inheritance() to walk base_clause and class_interface_clause child nodes. Wire into get_language_info() and get_ts_language() in mod.rs, add 'php' to EXTENSION_MAP and supported_languages() in lang.rs, add tree-sitter-php 0.25.2 to workspace.dependencies and crates/aptu-coder-core/Cargo.toml. Unit tests verify query compilation and element matching; integration test verifies analyze_file/analyze_directory/analyze_module on .php file.
pros: Follows established pattern from Java and Swift handlers
Covers all declaration kinds (functions, methods, classes, interfaces, traits, enums) in single ELEMENT_QUERY
extract_inheritance() handles both extends and implements clauses
DEFUSE_QUERY enables def-use analysis for PHP code
Full test coverage (unit + integration) ensures correctness
Minimal changes to registry files (mod.rs, lang.rs, Cargo.toml)
cons: Requires careful grammar inspection to get base_clause/class_interface_clause field names correct
DEFUSE_QUERY pattern needs validation against PHP-specific identifier scoping rules
Integration test must handle HTML-embedded PHP edge case (<?php ... ?> tags)

approaches.name: Minimal Handler (No Inheritance)
approaches.description: Create php.rs with only ELEMENT_QUERY, CALL_QUERY, REFERENCE_QUERY, IMPORT_QUERY, and empty DEFUSE_QUERY. Skip extract_inheritance() entirely (set to None in LanguageInfo). Wire into registry as above. Simpler implementation but loses inheritance analysis capability.
pros: Faster implementation; no extract_inheritance() logic needed
Still captures all declaration kinds and calls
cons: Loses inheritance information (extends/implements) that users may need
Inconsistent with Java/Swift/Kotlin handlers which all have extract_inheritance()
DEFUSE_QUERY omission means no def-use analysis
Does not meet issue acceptance criteria (extract_inheritance required)

approaches.name: Phased Approach (Queries First, Handlers Later)
approaches.description: Implement php.rs with all five queries and extract_inheritance() in phase 1. Wire into registry and add unit tests. In phase 2 (separate PR), add integration tests and README update. Allows validation of queries before committing to full integration.
pros: Decouples query validation from integration testing
Easier to iterate on query patterns if tree-sitter grammar inspection reveals surprises
Can gather feedback on queries before full integration
cons: Requires two PRs instead of one
Issue acceptance criteria require full integration in one PR

recommendation: Approach 1 (Full OO Handler with Inheritance). It follows the established pattern from Java and Swift, meets all issue acceptance criteria, and provides complete feature coverage (element extraction, call analysis, inheritance tracking, def-use analysis). The medium complexity is justified by the thoroughness of the result. Start with Step 2 of the issue's suggested approach: parse a small PHP sample with the grammar, list node kinds and fields, and confirm each against php/src/node-types.json. This de-risks the query writing phase. Then write and unit-test the five queries before wiring into the registry.

r"
(function_definition
  name: (name) @func_name) @function
(method_declaration
  name: (name) @method_name) @function
(class_declaration
  name: (name) @class_name) @class
(interface_declaration
  name: (name) @interface_name) @class
(trait_declaration
  name: (name) @trait_name) @class
(enum_declaration
  name: (name) @enum_name) @class
"
inheritance_walk_citation: From tree-sitter-php grammar (php/src/node-types.json and common/define-grammar.js): class_declaration has three fields: attributes (optional), body (required, type declaration_list), and name (required, type name). Inheritance is NOT a field of class_declaration; instead, base_clause and class_interface_clause are sibling child nodes (not fields). To extract inheritance: (1) walk the class_declaration node's children to find base_clause nodes; (2) for each base_clause, extract its named children which are name nodes representing the extended class; (3) walk to find class_interface_clause nodes; (4) for each class_interface_clause, extract its named children (name nodes) representing implemented interfaces. The grammar rule base_clause: $ => seq(keyword('extends'), commaSep1($._name)) and class_interface_clause: $ => seq(keyword('implements'), commaSep1($._name)) show that these nodes contain comma-separated name nodes as their children.
